context: Amazon Leadership Principles-structured work examples document, circa May 2018 (covers Jan 2017 – May 2018). Not a resume — a detailed evidence portfolio organized by Amazon LP dimensions: Deliver Results, Earn Trust, Bias for Action, Dive Deep, Hire & Develop the Best, Vocally Self-Critical. Contains specific ticket numbers, project appendix with HLD/LLD links, quantified impact metrics. Used for performance review / promotion calibration at Amazon TRMS.
raw_text:
=== DELIVER RESULTS (DESIGN & CODING) ===

1. Successfully delivered impactful projects in time requiring design, stake-holder management & coding: SVA OneAccountPerCustomer check, RiskProfileEvaluation (RiPE) of Fortress, XML Feed Migration & QueryGeneration & backfill tool for Automated Catalog System. Able to evaluate multiple options, call out pros and cons & take the most tech-relevant & stake-holder-friendly path. Proactively calls out any tech-debt incurred & articulates a step-by-step plan of mitigating it in phases. Keen eye for scaling, integration, fault-tolerance, acceptance criteria as NFRs.

2. On multiple occasions automated manual tasks & achieved results:
- Automated re-opening of 5297 closed herd workflows
- Automated ASIN pulls from RetailCatalogService and backfilled close to 1.9 billion ASINs across 12 different marketplaces and two different categories into EDX

3. Supported multiple client onboarding via clearly articulated SOPs & on-boarding docs:
- 29 successful client migrations for the XML Feed Migration project
- 6 successful client migrations for the RiPE project, with minimal SDE efforts

=== EARN TRUST (AWAY TEAM MODEL PROJECTS) ===

1. Is a part of IndiaPayments TRMS-Away team and has worked on 5 key away-team projects:
- Amazon India PPI Launch (StoredValueAccount/AmazonPay)
- RiskDocument creation & EvaluateRisk API of RiPE
- VariableComparisonTool enhancements

2. Proactively reaches out to stakeholders to understand possible paths. Meticulous in documenting requirements & scope. Maintains a wiki of MoMs with stakeholders, follows up consistently on action items, maintains task-list with start/end dates, dependencies, owner & completion artefacts. Extremely transparent in keeping stakeholders informed about status, risks, mitigation plans.

=== BIAS FOR ACTION ===

1. AbuseCOPS ruleset migration, QMS enablement for India — taken quick decisions & delivered in time to unblock dependencies.

2. Critical firefights handled independently:
- TT: 0128828360 — Amazon Pay PPI general availability launch was blocked because it was not whitelisted as a valid payment instrument. Diagnosed payment instrument type wrongly sent. Collaborated with INPayment team, solved end-end.
- TT: 0121783939 — BSF client migration caused a rebound effect; debug-console portal started failing to show pages. Stepped in, identified the issue, and fixed it before it escalated. Appreciated by the on-call during sprint retrospective.
- TT: 0128972298 — Manual investigation load saw an increase of 6.4k investigations in 3hrs duration. Sev-2 cut during non-office hours. Identified the issue, took corrective steps & ensured such incidents never happen again.

=== DIVE DEEP ===

1. AbusePreventionService optimizations:
- Analyzed Profiler (profiler.amazon.com) data for AbusePreventionService
- Identified root-causes for high CPU consuming cycles
- Made effective code changes to reduce CPU cycle usage on non-business logic code
- Impact: GC time reduced from 15% to 2.42%, improvement in supported TPS by 20%

2. IMR (Infrastructure/Machine Resource) reductions:
a. 2017 Dec hardware optimization: Released unused hardware, replaced old-generation hardware with new generation. Saved $23,000 per year in hardware costs.
b. APS & AbuseCOPS 2018 Prime-day scaling: Ran FLO tests, benchmarked hosts correctly, right-sized fleet. Saved $12,344.16 per year in hardware cost.

=== HIRE & DEVELOP THE BEST ===

1. Created multiple SDE onboarding pages:
a. ACSCS: Structured on-boarding with repository of high-quality content. Still used for all SDE on-boarding into ACSCS team.
b. TRMS SVA specific on-boarding page to help developers onboard to new projects quickly.
c. 1st week non-tech onboarding guide — reduces time from 1 week to about 2 days.

2. Created TRMS-INPay On-call helpbook for most common on-call questions & solutions.

3. Introduced Scaling for Development process within TRMS to identify the right Scrum process & adopt them. Team task completion rate improved from 50% to 85%.

4. Facilitator of Scrum Workshop & Agile Product Ownership workshop:
- 3 scrum workshops, reaching about 90 participants
- 1 agile product ownership workshop, reaching 10 participants
- One of 3 scrum facilitators in India recognized by EngineeringExcellence team
- One of 3 agile product ownership workshop facilitators in India recognized by EngineeringExcellence team

5. Mentored interns, SDE-1s & SDE-2s. Tech-reviewer for 3 promo docs of L4 to L5 promotions — all positive conversions.

6. Hiring: 68 interviews in 18 months. Created interview question bank used in 14 weekend interview events.

7. Created legendary bookmark page & troubleshooting page referred more than 1000 times.

=== VOCALLY SELF-CRITICAL ===

1. RDPS project implementation was called out as one of the projects that did not reach its completion. Exploratory nature of project, no clients or end goal. Expectation was not set at early stage. Has sought out help in clearly defining expectations on projects being worked on.

2. Bias for action on ticket 0128263358 — multiple back-and-forth, ultimately resulting in a code change. Acknowledged as an issue but confirmed consulting senior team members during back-and-forth. Not a recurrent issue — independently solved 43 tickets after this and was appreciated for bias-for-action taken in on-calls. Has sought out help in context setting of existing services.

=== APPENDIX — DELIVER RESULTS ===

1. RiskDocument for EvaluateRisk API of Fortress:
- Context: Create generic document acting as context & payload carrier for clients onboarding to Fortress (fraud/abuse detection platform), generic across multiple clients & different use-cases
- Delivered: Designed & implemented RiskDocument. Design approved by SDE-3, principal & samurai group.
- Artefacts: Use-case, Prototype, HLD, RiskDocumentModelCode, ClientHandlerCode, Integration test
- Impact: Launched first version of RiPE API on Fortress for CS-Tech use-case. EvaluateRisk API currently supports 6 clients, RiskDocument structure unchanged since launch.

2. Tool for bulk action on StoredValueAccount (SVA / AmazonPay) Investigations:
- Context: Just after AmazonPay India launch in July 2017, TRMS investigators understaffed. Backlog of 5927 investigations couldn't be attended. AmazonPay account creation blocked because SLA had passed.
- Delivered: Designed & implemented command-line tool to take taskIds of investigations & open them for investigators. Implementation done in record time.
- Artefacts: Use-case & design wiki, Code
- Impact: Tool handled 5927 blocked tasks. Project reported as successfully delivered in-time in weekly report. Tool so generically written it was re-used & extended to support another use-case.

3. XML Feed Migration by consistent XML to JSON Parser:
- Context: Ion generated from XML feeds was inconsistent, preventing indexing in Elasticsearch and writing reliable transformation code using aliasPath.
- Delivered: Designed, coded and introduced process to self-service migration of inconsistent ion generated via XML feed to consistent ion generation.
- Artefacts: XML Feed Migration Strategy, Bulk Migrator Tool Code, Self-service wiki
- Impact: 29 feed providers migrated using self-service tool without SDE involvement.

4. RCSQueryGeneration Tool:
- Context: Generate value metrics query results across 12 marketplaces to identify how many ASINs were resultant of automated feed parsing.
- Delivered: Designed & wrote tool to query RCS, process results and upload into EDX warehouse. Created DJS jobs running daily. Helped back-fill data from 1970 till present.
- Artefacts: QueryGenerationTool, Backfill jobs, DJS Job1, DJS Job2
- Impact: Backfill jobs processed 930 Million vendor contribution responses, 1.1 Billion create-by-date responses. DJS job continuously processes approx 30,000 ASINs per day.

=== APPENDIX — EARN TRUST ===

1. SVA OAOC Launch: Conceptualized and led the OneAccountOneCustomer fraud use-case for the launch of AmazonPay in March 2017 (family & friends launch) and general availability July 2017. Handled end-end processes including requirements gathering, design, stakeholder communications, coding 1 & coding 2, on-boarding. Appreciated by directors of TRMS.

2. VariableComparisonTool Enhancement: Improved reporting details of VariableComparisonTool that reported variable mismatches between FRS (legacy service) and Fortress (replacement service) for SVA use-case. Made generic code changes (GLS filtering, variable filtering, generate sample OrderIds, control decimal point precision) to introduce options for custom reports. SDE effort reduction by 60%.

3. S-Team goal: Contributed towards resolving major SIM validating mismatch of variables evaluated by FRS and Fortress in Inline evaluation.

4. RiPE API: Worked with Fortress team to facilitate initial launch of RiPE API for CS-Tech use-case. Presented RiPE to director Anand (anandva@). Developed and delivered components for the CS-Tech use-case.

5. FDPS Client Analysis: Analyzed clients calling FDPS. Created follow-up wiki to see if clients still have dependencies on FDPS. Intent to see how to support FDPS hosting RiskDocument instead of FraudDocument, and analyze chance of gracefully deprecating FDPS and moving to new data-store (RDPS).

=== APPENDIX — BIAS FOR ACTION ===

1. AbuseCOPS stage-3 to stage-1 COD suppression rule migration: Identified root cause of COD suppression slippages during flash-sales. Proposed solution to migrate suppression rules from stage-3 to stage-1 of AbuseCOPS to ensure evaluation results computed within 250 milliseconds.

2. QMS enablement for IN SVA: Enabling Queue Management Service for IN Retail. During peak times (Diwali, Christmas, New Year, Cyber Monday), SVA runs promotional offers resulting in increased traffic and increased investigations in queues with very low SLA timelines (1hr). Hard to adhere to SLAs with high volumes.

=== APPENDIX — DIVE DEEP ===

1. AbusePreventionService: Analyzed Profiler data, identified root-causes for high CPU consuming cycles, made code changes. GC time reduced from 15% to 2.42%, improvement in supported TPS by 20%.

2. IMR reductions:
a. 2017 Dec: Released unused hardware, replaced old-generation with new generation EC2 hosts. Saved $23,000/year.
b. APS & AbuseCOPS Prime-day 2018: Ran FLO tests, right-sized fleet, saved $12,344.16/year.

=== APPENDIX — HIRE & DEVELOP THE BEST ===

1. ACSCS onboarding: Structured approach for on-boarding new team member, repository of high-quality content. Still used for all SDE on-boarding into ACSCS team.
2. TRMS SVA specific on-boarding page.
3. 1st week non-tech onboarding guide — reduces setup time from 1 week to ~2 days.
4. TRMS-INPay On-call helpbook.
5. Scaling for Development process within TRMS. Team completion rate from 50% to 85%.
6. Facilitator: 3 scrum workshops (~90 participants), 1 agile PO workshop (~10 participants). One of 3 recognized by EngineeringExcellence team in India.
7. Mentored interns & SDE-1s/SDE-2s.
8. 68 interviews in 18 months. Question bank used in 14 weekend events.
9. Legendary bookmark & troubleshooting pages — referred more than 1000 times.

=== AWARDS ===
- 1st place in ACSCS 2016 Hackathon
- TRMS Zeus Team Award for exceptional project delivery (RiPE)
- TRMS Spot Award for contributing towards team process improvements via Scaling for Development guidelines
